items.text: Life outcomes are primarily determined by:

options.B: Effort matters most, with some luck involved
options.C: Complex mix of effort, circumstance, and chance
options.D: Structural factors and luck matter more than individual effort

items.text: Two equally talented people start businesses—one succeeds wildly, one fails. The difference is primarily:

options.A: Effort, persistence, and quality of decisions
options.B: Skill differences that weren't initially apparent
options.C: Complex interaction of ability, timing, and luck
options.D: Market timing and circumstances beyond their control
options.E: Random luck—success is mostly being in the right place at the right time

items.text: "You make your own luck" vs. "Success is mostly being in the right place at the right time." Which is closer to truth?

options.A: You make your own luck—outcomes follow from effort
options.B: You significantly influence your luck through preparation
options.C: Both are partially true—effort and circumstance both matter
options.D: Timing and circumstances matter more than effort
options.E: Right place, right time—success is largely circumstantial
